title: Social Sim Arena weekly bundle
description: One batch of questions, all due at one deadline. Produced by tools/emit_bundle.py from the reviewed rounds in questions/season0.json; never from unreviewed candidates. Closed by design: adding a field means editing this file first, or every consumer written against schema_version 1.0.0 sees a payload it was not promised.

instant.description: UTC, seconds precision, trailing Z. Every timestamp in this repository is written this way; a local-time or offset-bearing string is rejected rather than parsed, because a deadline read in the wrong zone is a submission window that silently moves.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this payload shape. Bumped when a consumer would have to change; a bundle whose version a client does not know must be refused, not guessed at.

batch_id.description: ssa.batches.batch_of(lock_at) for every round in the bundle. The date is the deadline's date.

deadline.description: When every forecast in this bundle is due: Monday 12:00Z. This is ssa.batches.effective_deadline, NOT a round's lock_at. Rounds still lock at release - 48h, 0 to 7 days after this moment; that is the arena's clock, not the participant's. Filing early is allowed and costs nothing, because the deadline is common to everyone.

published_at.description: deadline - 7 days: when the batch is handed to entrants. Publication is a bundle concern, not a validity rule -- a round added after this moment is still governed by the deadline computed from its lock, it just arrives after entrants read the bundle.

questions.description: The rounds in this batch, in lock order. May be empty: a week with no reviewed round locking in it is a real state, not an error.

round_id.description: Matches a round in questions/season0.json, and is the directory a submission file goes in.

tracker.description: The upstream that publishes the answer.

series.description: The registered series id, or the ranking series for a list round.

question.description: The exact quantity in words: denominator, answer options, population, and for a ranking round the week and the eligible universe. An entrant is graded on this wording.

unit.description: A number without a unit cannot be scored against anything.

target_type.description: Which shape the answer takes, and therefore which of cells/items is populated. A bundle mixes all three.

lock_at.description: release - 48h. Never show this to a participant as the deadline; show `deadline`.

horizon_days.description: Deadline to lock, in days, to one decimal. Varies across a batch and is identical for every entrant, which is what makes it a property of the question worth reporting rather than a confound between competitors.

resolve.description: How the round will be settled. Part of the question, not documentation.

cells.description: The population cells a profile_energy round asks about. Empty for every other shape -- present-but-empty rather than absent, so a consumer iterating a mixed batch never hits a KeyError.

items.description: The closed candidate set a ranking_list round orders. Empty for other shapes, and also empty for the Wikipedia top-10 round, whose answer is drawn from every article on the wiki -- naming a candidate list there would be a different and much easier question.
